chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Ibn Faddal, from Ali ibn Ya'qub, from Marwan ibn Muslim, from Muhammad ibn Shurayh, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the exiting of women on the two Eids.
He said: No, except for the old woman upon whom is her two footwears (manqalahayn) - meaning the two loose indoor shoes.

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
key_terms.الْعِيدَيْنِ: The two Eids (Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha)
key_terms.مَنقَلَاهَا: Two footwears, specifically loose indoor shoes or slippers worn by women

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on women going out for Eid prayers according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In *Mani al-Akhbar*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this ruling from Imam al-Sadi’ (AS) distinguishing between general female modesty and the specific exception for elderly women, who are permitted to exit in loose indoor footwear (*manqalahayn*) due to their reduced need for strict outer covering. This highlights the juristic principle that age and physical condition can modify the standard requirements of *hijab* and public appearance, emphasizing practical ease (*rukhas*) within the framework of modesty.
